content:
Why it matters IntStream.range(0, n).forEach(...) takes an IntConsumer, which cannot throw checked exceptions. The usual workaround wraps and unwraps.
STREAMS IntStream.range(0, 3).forEach(i -> { try { Files.createFile(path(i)); } catch (IOException e) { throw new UncheckedIOException(e); } }); JAVA-REPEAT repeat(3, i -> Files.createFile(path(i))); // throws IOException How the type is inferred repeat is declared <E extends Throwable> ... throws E. The compiler picks E from what the lambda throws:
Throws nothing checked: E is RuntimeException; nothing to declare. Throws one checked type: E is that type, for example IOException. Throws several: E is their common supertype, often Exception. Catch inside the action if you need them apart. A failure stops the loop repeat(5, i -> { ran.add(i); if (i == 1) throw new IOException("ERROR!"); }); // ran == [0, 1]; the IOException reaches the caller 0ran 1threw 2skipped 3skipped 4skipped Keep going after a failure To run every iteration regardless, catch inside the action and collect what failed.
List<IOException> failures = new ArrayList<>(); repeat(5, i -> { try { Files.createFile(path(i)); } catch (IOException e) { failures.add(e); } });
lede: The action can throw a checked exception. It reaches the caller unchanged, and the loop stops.
title: Checked exceptions

content:
Breaking change. The new repeat returns void; it no longer collects results into a list. Steps 1 Bump the version
<version>0.0.9 1.0.1</version> 2 Switch to the static import
import io.github.repeat.Repeat; import static io.github.repeat.Repeat.*; 3 Rewrite each call
Result ignored
Repeat.of().times(3).repeat(i -> { send(i); return null; }); repeat(3, i -> send(i)); Result used: collect it yourself
List<String> ids = Repeat.of().times(3).repeat(i -> "id-" + i); List<String> ids = new ArrayList<>(); repeat(3, i -> ids.add("id-" + i)); Removed types 0.0.9 1.0.0 and later Repeat.of() → RepeatContext Repeat.repeat(int, IndexedAction) RepeatCallback<T, E> IndexedAction<E> (no return value) doWithRepeat(int) accept(int) RepeatOperations, RepeatTemplate Removed; no replacement needed
lede: 1.0.0 replaces the builder with one static method. 0.0.9 and earlier used Repeat.of().times(n).repeat(...).
title: Migrating from 0.x

content:
Summary Type Member Description Repeat repeat(int, IndexedAction<E>) Runs the action times times with the zero-based index. IndexedAction<E> accept(int) The action your lambda implements; may throw E. Repeat final class since 1.0.0
Kotlin-style function for running code multiple times. Designed for static import. Holds only static members; it cannot be instantiated.
public final class Repeat repeat public static <E extends Throwable> void repeat( final int times, final IndexedAction<E> action) throws E Executes the action the given number of times, passing the zero-based index of each iteration. Like Kotlin’s repeat, a zero or negative times runs nothing.
TYPE PARAMETERS E — the exception type the action may throw; inferred from the lambda. PARAMETERS times — the number of times to execute the actionaction — the action to execute; receives the index THROWS E — if the action fails; remaining iterations are not executed Behavior When Result times > 0 Calls action.accept(i) for i = 0 … times - 1, in order, on the calling thread. times <= 0 Does nothing. The action is never called. action throws at index k Indexes 0 … k ran. The exception propagates unchanged, not wrapped. action == null NullPointerException on the first iteration; nothing if times <= 0. Examples import static io.github.repeat.Repeat.*; // method reference: collect the indexes 0, 1, 2 List<Integer> indexes = new ArrayList<>(); repeat(3, indexes::add); // ignore the index StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder(); repeat(2, i -> out.append("x")); // "xx" View sourceJavadoc: Repeat
IndexedAction<E> functional interface since 1.0.0
An action that receives the zero-based index of the current iteration. You rarely name it: a lambda or method reference passed to repeat becomes one.
@FunctionalInterface public interface IndexedAction<E extends Throwable> TYPE PARAMETERS E — the exception type accept may throw. For a lambda that throws nothing checked, the compiler infers RuntimeException, so callers declare nothing. accept void accept(int index) throws E PARAMETERS index — zero-based index of the current iteration THROWS E — any exception the action raises Ways to write one Form Example E is Lambda i -> log.info("run " + i) RuntimeException Method reference indexes::add RuntimeException Throwing lambda i -> Files.delete(paths[i]) IOException Stored in a variable IndexedAction<IOException> a = i -> ...; as declared View sourceJavadoc: IndexedAction
lede: Package io.github.repeat: one class, one functional interface. Generated Javadoc for every version is on javadoc.io.

content:
Requirements Java 8 or later. No runtime dependencies. Install Maven <dependency> <groupId>io.github.java-repeat</groupId> <artifactId>repeat</artifactId> <version>1.0.1</version> </dependency> Gradle implementation("io.github.java-repeat:repeat:1.0.1") Your first call import static io.github.repeat.Repeat.*; repeat(3, i -> System.out.println("attempt " + i)); Output
attempt 0 attempt 1 attempt 2 The lambda receives the zero-based index of each iteration. A zero or negative count does nothing.
Throwing checked exceptions The action may throw. The exception type is inferred, so the caller declares it as if it had written the loop itself.
void createFiles() throws IOException { repeat(3, i -> Files.createFile(Paths.get("file-" + i))); } If an iteration throws, the remaining iterations do not run. See Checked exceptions. Next API reference: the full contract of repeat(int, IndexedAction). Migrating from 0.x: if you used Repeat.of().times(n).
lede: Add one dependency, statically import Repeat.*, and call repeat.
